te.title: The temperatures go crazy
te.sit: First start-up of a new unit; it has run well for several shifts. About an hour ago the new operator raised the column pressure set point by 0.1 MPa. About 20 minutes later the tray temperatures began to swing, and in the last few minutes they have gone crazy and the bottoms level has started to fall. You have just been called. It is cold (−1 °C).

te.title: The feed flow will not settle
te.sit: Unit lined out after an instrument upgrade last night (new remote I/O cabinet). Since then FIC-201 swings between roughly 10 and 75 m³/h and the whole column follows.

te.title: The flare is bigger than usual
te.sit: Unit lined out. The shift supervisor says the flare has been growing for the last half hour; the board shows the column pressure below set point.

te.title: The reboiler valve keeps opening
te.sit: Unit lined out. Over the shift TV-208 has been opening further and PI-205 has been rising, although the products are on spec.

te.title: Everything goes to zero
te.sit: Unit lined out. A few seconds ago most flows on the board went to zero and several alarms came in at once.

te.title: The debutanizer gets no feed
te.sit: Unit lined out. The debutanizer operator phones: their feed from C-201 has stopped.

te.title: Pressure control running out of vent
te.sit: Unit lined out. PV-210 has been opening further every day this week and the fuel gas header is getting richer.

te.title: Bottoms off spec after the feed changed
te.sit: Unit lined out. Upstream changed its feed slate an hour ago. The debutanizer says there is too much propane in its feed.

te.title: The column has lost stages
te.sit: Unit lined out after a pressure surge last night. The bottoms have been drifting off spec and the bottom temperature is lower than usual, although the steam has not changed much.

te.title: ΔP high and bottoms off spec
te.sit: Unit lined out. PDI-212 has jumped and the bottoms analyzer is climbing.

te.title: A hot afternoon
te.sit: Unit lined out. It is getting hotter and the cooling tower is struggling.

te.title: Nothing happens when the load changes
te.sit: Unit lined out. Upstream will raise its rate shortly and you will take the extra feed.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 The temperatures go crazy (Depropanizer C-201)
meta.sit: First start-up of a new unit; it has run well for several shifts. About an hour ago the new operator raised the column pressure set point by 0.1 MPa. About 20 minutes later the tray temperatures began to swing, and in the last few minutes they have gone crazy and the bottoms level has started to fall. You have just been called. It is cold (−1 °C).

0.1.unit: C-201 is a 27-tray depropanizer: a C3/C4 feed from the upstream unit runs into the feed surge drum V-201 (24.8 m³, no level control in rev A — only the gauge glass LG-201 in the field), is pumped by P-201A (motor; P-201B steam-turbine spare, auto-started by FSLL-201) through FIC-201 / FV-201 and the steam preheater E-201 (TIC-202) onto tray 18. The thermosyphon reboiler E-203 (TIC-208 on tray 8 → steam TV-208) and the water-cooled total condenser E-202 with reflux drum V-202 and P-202A/B make propane overhead (AI-219, C4+ ≤ 2.5 mol %) and C4+ bottoms to the debutanizer on pressure (AI-220, C3 ≤ 2.0 mol %). PIC-210 holds the top at 1.70 MPa g by venting non-condensables to fuel gas through PV-210; PSV-201 protects the column. Design: feed 60 m³/h, propane 32.1 m³/h, bottoms 27.8 m³/h, margin 5 809 $/h.

rows.what: Tray temperatures swinging: TIC-208 65.2–97.8 °C in the last 20 min, 94.6 °C now (SP 76.9)
Feed FI-201 0.00 m³/h with FIC-201 output 100 % (SP 60)
Sump LIC-202 38.9 % and falling, bottoms FI-202 12.3 m³/h (design 27.8)
Top pressure PIC-210 1.494 MPa g against SP 1.80 (raised from 1.70 at −00:48:10); alarms PIC-210 LO and TIC-208 HI
Event log: P-201B started by FSLL-201 at −00:24:57; P-201A and P-201B reported 'lost suction' at −00:24:52 and −00:02:28

0.4.ctx: First start-up of a new unit; it has run well for several shifts. The new operator raised the PIC-210 set point by 0.1 MPa at −00:48:10. Night shift, ambient −1 °C. The previous rounds log has V-201 at 64 % (−08:49) and 40 % (−04:49). No maintenance today.

R.1.p: A depropanizer splits propane from butanes by relative volatility: the vapour from the reboiler and the liquid reflux set the separation, and the tray temperatures read the composition at the column pressure (tray 8 at 76.9 °C at 1.70 MPa g). Everything starts with the feed: no feed, no profile — the trays and the sump empty and the loops chase a column that has nothing to separate. Upstream of the column the feed path is a balance: V-201 has no level control in rev A, so its level integrates (supply − FIC-201 flow); a centrifugal pump needs liquid above its suction, and with too little submergence it vortexes, fills with gas and runs on without head (gas-bound) until it is primed.

R.2.eq: dV/dt = F_up − F_FIC-201      Δt_empty = V_held / (F_FIC-201 − F_up)      T_tray ≈ f(x, P)

rows.info: First start-up of a new unit; it has run well for several shifts. About an hour ago the new operator raised the column pressure set point by 0.1 MPa. About 20 minutes later the tray temperatures began to swing, and in the last few minutes they have gone crazy and the bottoms level has started to fall. You have just been called. It is cold (−1 °C).
“The pressure change did it — put it back to 1.70.”
“The drum was fine at the last round.”
Alarms PIC-210 LO and TIC-208 HI; FI-201 0.00 m³/h

1.3.safn: Top 1.494 MPa g, falling — far from PSV-201 (1.80); sump 38.9 %, LSLL-202 trips at 5 % (falling ≈ 1 %/min)
1.3.envn: PSV-201 tail pipe at ambient: no flaring now (it lifted on and off before the call)
1.3.eqn: Two pumps running without liquid: seal and bearing damage within minutes
1.3.prodn: No feed: margin −5 809 $/h; the debutanizer loses its feed
1.3.ttl: ≈ 30 min to the LSLL-202 trip at the present sump fall; pump seals now

1.4.why: The feed is lost and the loops chase an emptying column; the gas-bound pumps are being damaged. No relief or trip limit is close yet, so an ESD is not needed: park the column, protect the pumps, then find why the feed path lost liquid.
1.4.park: TIC-208, FIC-204, LIC-202, LIC-203 to MAN at their present outputs; PIC-210 SP back to 1.70 MPa g; FIC-201 MAN 30 %; stop both gas-bound feed pumps.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable state that stops a problem growing while you investigate (here: loops in MAN, column held, pumps stopped).
1.5.tc: A consequence for people, environment or equipment arrives before the diagnosis is done unless you act now (here: pumps running dry, sump heading for the trip).

1.6.p: The column runs on its feed, and the feed path is a balance: V-201 level integrates supply − draw, and a pump only delivers while liquid covers its suction.

ppl.msg: Feed lost, both feed pumps without head; column safe-parked; not reversing the pressure change blind
Feed pumps (noise, PG-203A/B), LG-201 and the rounds log, PSV-201 tail pipe
What are you sending to V-201 now, and since when?
Our bottoms will be low for about an hour

1.7.reply: The depropanizer has lost its feed; the column is parked safely and the pumps are stopped. We are checking the feed drum and the pumps and expect feed back within about 15 minutes, products on spec within the hour. We report again in 30 minutes.

FIC-201 OUT ≈ 40 % at 60 m³/h. V-201 24.8 m³ horizontal drum, no level transmitter in rev A; FSLL-201 starts P-201B below 15 m³/h.

3.2.n: Supply 57 m³/h (upstream) against 60 m³/h drawn by FIC-201: 3 m³/h out of a drum without level control. The rounds log shows 64 → 40 % in 4 h = 7.5 m³ of the 24.8 m³ horizontal drum, ≈ 1.9 m³/h net — the same order: the drum has been emptying all shift and nobody could see it on the DCS. Once the level reaches the suction the pump vortexes and gas-binds; FSLL-201 then starts P-201B, which drains the rest and binds in turn.

3.5.tree:
TOP: feed to C-201 lost, temperatures swing
 OR — No liquid reaches FV-201
    OR — V-201 empty: supply < draw (no level control) → pumps gas-bound
    OR — Suction line blocked (cold weather)
 OR — Liquid blocked downstream of the pumps
    OR — FV-201 / XV-201 shut
 OR — The measurement is wrong (FT-201 low)
 OR — The column itself upset
    OR — Pressure set-point step
    OR — Reboiler / steam
    OR — Condenser / inerts
3.5.cut: Single-element cut sets. Pumps without head with LG-201 low point to the first branch; dead-headed pumps would point to the second.

rows.st: “The pressure change did it — put it back to 1.70.”
rows.how: Not supported: the feed held 60 m³/h for many minutes after the step; a set point cannot stop a pump

rows.st: “The drum was fine at the last round.”
rows.how: Not supported: rounds log 64 → 40 %; LG-201 now low

3.8.n: The pressure step at −00:48:10 is the only logged human change and the obvious suspect; it brought the top close to the PSV set point but cannot stop a pump. The change nobody logged is the supply: upstream runs a little lower today (57 m³/h), and in rev A that is invisible on the DCS.

3.10.n: Agreed: the column follows the feed; the feed follows the liquid at the pump suction.

3.11.n: The statement names only the symptom

4.1.ideas:
Feed drum ran down, pumps gas-bound
Pressure set-point step
PIC-210 transmitter wrong
FV-201 or XV-201 shut, FT-201 low
Reboiler / steam supply
Cold weather: line or preheater blocked
Condenser / inerts

rows.act: Laboratory samples of feed and bottoms
rows.why: Hours and thousands of dollars; the analyzers and the field answer the question

rows.why: Free; kills or keeps three hypotheses

rows.why: Protects the pumps and holds the column away from the trips

5.1.proof: T-2 (feed lost before the swings), T-3 (pumps without head, LG-201 low, rounds falling), T-4 (upstream 57 m³/h), T-5 (primed pump delivers at once); Ev-3, Ev-4, Ev-9, Ev-10, Ev-11, Ev-12, Ev-14
5.1.mech: Upstream sends 57 m³/h → FIC-201 draws 60 m³/h → V-201 (no level control in rev A) loses about 3 m³/h for hours → the level reaches the pump suction → P-201A vortexes and gas-binds (−00:24:52) → FSLL-201 starts P-201B (−00:24:57), which drains the rest and gas-binds (−00:02:28) → FI-201 0, FV-201 100 % → the column loses its feed: trays and sump empty, the loops chase the profile and the temperatures swing. The PIC-210 step at −00:48:10 only moved the top close to the PSV set point.

rows.opt: Wait for V-201 to refill above the suction, prime P-201A, start it, FIC-201 AUTO at the upstream rate (57 m³/h)
Put PIC-210 back to 1.70 MPa g only
Rev B now (LT-201 on the DCS with LAL/LAH-201, FAL-201), rev C at the turnaround (LIC-201 cascaded onto FIC-201)

rows.step: Tell the supervisor and upstream: feed lost, drum low, column parked
Safe-park: loops to MAN, PIC-210 SP 1.70, FIC-201 MAN 30 %, stop both pumps
Wait for LG-201 ≥ 35 % (above the suction); prime P-201A; start it; FIC-201 AUTO at 57 m³/h
If P-201A rattles again or PG-203A stays low, stop it and wait longer before priming again
Column loops back to AUTO; watch AI-220 and TIC-208 until on spec
Rev B in service under MOC; LG-201 read every hour until then

rows.act: Safe-park: TIC-208, FIC-204, LIC-202, LIC-203 to MAN; PIC-210 SP 1.70; FIC-201 MAN 30 %; both pumps stopped; P-201A casing vented
LIC-202, LIC-203, FIC-204 (49 m³/h), TIC-208 (76.9 °C) back to AUTO
Rev B in service: LT-201 on the DCS (temporary, MOC)

5.7.n: The stripping section refilled with light feed: bottoms C3 AI-220 peaked at 7.40 mol % at 00:12:42 (spec 2.0) and TIC-208 ran low; both products on spec from 00:42:39. At 01:39:42: feed 56.8 m³/h, top 1.700 MPa g, tray 8 76.8 °C, AI-219 1.32, AI-220 0.86 mol %, LI-201 steady at 36.4 %, margin 5 424 $/h at 57 m³/h feed. P-201B is still gas-bound: prime it before it is needed as the spare.

5.8.rule: When the feed is lost with the valve wide open and the pumps running, go to the drum and the pumps before you touch the column.

6.0.n: T-5 gave the predicted flow at once; the recovery took longer than hoped because the stripping section had to refill.

rows.m: Rev B: LT-201 on the DCS with LAL/LAH-201 and FAL-201 (a supply change becomes an alarm, not a lost feed)
Rev C at the turnaround: LIC-201 cascaded onto FIC-201 (averaging level control), so the column takes what upstream sends
Until rev B: LG-201 read and logged every hour; any falling trend reported to the board
Set-point changes on a new unit only with a reason in the log and the supervisor’s agreement

6.1.kpi: V-201 level trend (LI-201 % per hour), target |slope| < 1 %/h

rows.i: Feed back at the real supply; drum level now visible
Rev C will let the feed rate swing with upstream: the column must ride feed changes (slow, averaging level tuning)
One more transmitter to maintain and to trust (what if LT-201 fails?)

hz.cons: Pumps gas-bound, feed lost, column upset
hz.sg: LAL-201, FAL-201, rounds; rev C level control

hz.cons: Drum full, upstream backs up or relieves

hz.cause: LT-201 fails low → LIC-201 cuts FIC-201
hz.sg: FAL-201, LG-201 check, high/low clamp on the cascade

6.3.fut: Any vessel without level control integrates every flow mismatch; on a new unit, check where such inventories sit and how the operator sees them.

6.4.how: Without the diagnosis the obvious move (PIC-210 back, restart the pumps unprimed) would have left the feed off for at least another 2 h: 2 × 5 809 $/h margin saved, pump seals not replaced (assumed values).

6.5.again:
Read the history (negative time) before blaming the latest change.
Go to the field: gauge glass, pump noise and discharge gauge answered in minutes.
Safe-park first when equipment is being damaged.
6.5.never:
Never restart a gas-bound pump without priming it and covering its suction.
Never reverse a change only because it was the last one made.

evidence.text: FIC-201 reads 0.00 m³/h against its design value 60 m³/h, with its output at 100 % (design 40 %): FV-201 is wide open.

PIC-210 SP was raised 1.700 → 1.800 MPa g at −00:48:10. The feed held 60 m³/h for 16 min after the step; the top rose to 1.786 MPa g and PSV-201 lifted to the flare on and off from −00:40:10 to −00:04:40 (peak 402 Nm³/h at −00:21:10).
FIC-201 OUT crept up from 41.8 % to 44.5 % between −00:43:10 and −00:35:00 at a constant 60 m³/h; the feed first dipped below 58 m³/h at −00:31:50.
Event log: −00:24:57 FSLL-201 auto-started P-201B; −00:24:52 P-201A lost suction (casing full of gas); −00:02:28 P-201B lost suction. No operator action after the set-point change.

In the last 20 min TIC-208 swung 65.2–97.8 °C; at 00:00:30 tray 8 94.6 °C (design 76.9), feed tray TI-245 39.5 °C (design 65.8), sump LIC-202 38.9 % and falling, bottoms FI-202 12.3 m³/h (design 27.8).
PIC-210 1.494 and the independent PI-211 1.494 MPa g agree; the field gauge PG-211 reads 1.49 MPa g.
Steam header PI-207 450 kPa g (design 450), cooling water FI-216 330 m³/h (design 330), TI-214 14.9 °C — utilities on design (IS NOT candidates).
Feed preheat TIC-202 145.7 °C against 75 °C with TV-202 shut and no feed flowing through E-201.

Field, P-201A/B: P-201A running, shaft turning, loud rattling noise, casing cool, PG-203A 453 kPa g: no head. P-201B running, shaft turning, loud rattling noise, casing cool, PG-203B 453 kPa g: no head.
Field, V-201: Level in the glass ≈ 25 %; rounds log −08:49 64 %, −04:49 40 %. In rev A this level is not on the DCS.

evidence.text: V-201 balance from the rounds: 64 → 40 % in 4 h = 7.5 m³ of the 24.8 m³ drum ≈ 1.9 m³/h more out than in.
Upstream unit (telephone): "We are sending 57 m³/h to V-201, a little lower than usual today."
PSV-201 tail pipe at ambient temperature: the valve is shut.
T-5: with V-201 back to ≈ 35 % on LG-201, P-201A primed and started at 00:03:37: FI-201 0.1 → 54.1 m³/h within 5 s of AUTO, PG-203A 2388 kPa g, pump quiet.

hyp.cause: V-201 drained: less comes in than FIC-201 draws (no level control in rev A), so both feed pumps gas-bound
hyp.ifthen: If V-201 ran down, the pumps vortex and fill with gas one after the other: FIC-201 opens FV-201 to hold the rate, the spare starts on FSLL-201 and then also loses suction; the feed falls to zero and the column empties
hyp.key: FIC-201 OUT ↑ at constant flow before the loss; FSLL-201 start; pumps rattle with no head; LG-201 low; upstream < 60 m³/h
hyp.fals: LG-201 at a normal level, or a pump giving full head, or upstream sending 60 m³/h

hyp.cause: The PIC-210 set-point step (1.70 → 1.80 MPa g) upset the column and caused the swings
hyp.ifthen: If the pressure step did it, the swings start at the step and the feed is not affected: FI-201 stays at 60 m³/h, the profile shifts colder and settles
hyp.key: Swings from the step on; feed steady; PSV-201 lifting
hyp.fals: Feed held for many minutes after the step and the swings start when the feed is lost; a set point cannot stop a pump

hyp.cause: PIC-210 reads wrong: the pressure is not what the DCS shows
hyp.ifthen: If PIC-210 read wrong, the independent PI-211 and the field gauge PG-211 would disagree with it
hyp.fals: PI-211 and PG-211 agree with PIC-210

hyp.cause: Feed valve or feed instrument (FV-201 stuck shut, XV-201 shut, FT-201 failed low)
hyp.ifthen: If the valve or the meter were the problem, the pumps would be healthy: quiet, full discharge pressure against a shut valve, and the drum level normal
hyp.key: PG-203A/B high (dead-headed), pumps quiet, FV-201 position ≠ output
hyp.fals: Pumps rattling with no head; flow back as soon as a primed pump starts with nothing else changed

hyp.cause: Reboiler or steam problem (TV-208, steam supply) drives the tray temperatures
hyp.ifthen: If the heat input were the problem, TV-208 and FI-205 would move first and the steam header would be off; the feed would be unaffected
hyp.key: PI-207 off design; FI-205 change before TIC-208; feed steady
hyp.fals: Steam header on design; feed lost before the temperatures swing

hyp.cause: Cold weather: feed line or preheater blocked (−1 °C)
hyp.ifthen: If the feed line were blocked, the pumps would run dead-headed with full discharge pressure and the drum would fill up
hyp.key: PG-203 high, LG-201 rising, TIC-202 cold
hyp.fals: Pumps without head; LG-201 low; TIC-202 hot

hyp.cause: Overhead problem (condenser E-202, inerts, vent PV-210) behind the pressure change
hyp.ifthen: If the overhead were the problem, the cooling water or the vent would be off design and the pressure would move first, with the feed steady
hyp.key: FI-216/TI-214 off design, PV-210 open, pressure rising
hyp.fals: Cooling water on design, vent shut, pressure falling after the feed loss

tests.title: Compare PIC-210 with PI-211 and the field gauge PG-211
tests.move: Nothing moved: read PIC-210 and PI-211 on the DCS, ask the outside operator for PG-211 at the column top.

WH-3.note: PI-211 / PG-211 read higher than PIC-210 (the real pressure is not 1.49)

WH-1.note: all three agree; the low pressure is real (no feed vapour)

tests.kill: |PI-211 − PIC-210| > 0.02 MPa → WH-3 survives; within 0.01 MPa and PG-211 the same → WH-3 killed.

res.obs: PIC-210 1.494, PI-211 1.494 MPa g, PG-211 column top 1.49 MPa g: they agree.

tests.title: Trend review in negative time: feed, FIC-201 OUT, PIC-210 SP, tray 8
tests.move: Nothing moved: trends from −00:49 to now, event log.

WH-1.note: feed falls first (OUT creeps up, spare starts, both pumps lose suction), the temperatures swing after

WH-2.note: feed steady at 60 m³/h; the swings start at the pressure step

WH-5.note: feed steady; steam / TV-208 move first

tests.kill: Swings start at the step with the feed steady → WH-2 survives; feed lost before the swings → WH-2 and WH-5 killed.

res.obs: Feed held 60 m³/h for 16 min after the step; FIC-201 OUT 41.8 → 44.5 % meanwhile; P-201B started −00:24:57, P-201A lost suction −00:24:52, P-201B −00:02:28; TIC-208 swings 65–98 °C come after the feed falls.

tests.title: Field: look and listen at P-201A/B; read LG-201 and the rounds log
tests.move: Outside operator to the feed pumps and V-201: pump noise, discharge gauges PG-203A/B, gauge glass LG-201, rounds log.

WH-1.note: LG-201 low and falling in the rounds; pumps rattle, no head

WH-4.note: LG-201 normal; pumps quiet with full discharge pressure (dead-headed)

WH-6.note: LG-201 normal or rising; pumps dead-headed

tests.kill: Pumps without head and LG-201 low → WH-4 and WH-6 killed; LG-201 normal with high PG-203 → WH-1 killed.

res.obs: P-201A running, shaft turning, loud rattling noise, casing cool, PG-203A 453 kPa g: no head. P-201B running, shaft turning, loud rattling noise, casing cool, PG-203B 453 kPa g: no head. Level in the glass ≈ 25 %  Rounds log: −08:49 64 % · −04:49 40 %

tests.title: Telephone the upstream unit; outside operator checks the PSV-201 tail pipe
tests.move: Ask upstream what they send to V-201; feel the PSV-201 tail pipe (frosted or warm = passing).

WH-1.note: upstream sends less than the 60 m³/h FIC-201 draws

WH-2.note: PSV-201 still passing after lifting at the 1.80 set point

tests.kill: Upstream < 60 m³/h → WH-1 confirmed; PSV tail pipe at ambient → WH-2 has no lasting effect.

res.obs: Upstream unit: "We are sending 57 m³/h to V-201, a little lower than usual today." PSV-201 tail pipe at ambient temperature: the valve is shut.

tests.title: Prime P-201A once V-201 is above the suction, start it, FIC-201 to AUTO
tests.move: After the safe-park (00:02:35) and with LG-201 back to ≈ 35 %: vent the P-201A casing to flare until liquid shows, start P-201A (00:03:37), FIC-201 MAN 30 % → AUTO at 57 m³/h, the rate upstream sends.

WH-1.note: feed back to ≈ 55 m³/h within a minute; pump quiet, PG-203A > 2 000 kPa g

WH-4.note: still no flow: the valve or the meter is the problem

tests.kill: FI-201 > 40 m³/h within 2 min → WH-4 killed, WH-1 confirmed; FI-201 < 5 m³/h with the pump primed → WH-1 killed, stop the pump.
tests.stop: Stop P-201A at once if it rattles again, if PG-203A stays below 1 000 kPa g after 30 s, or if LG-201 falls below 15 %.
tests.back: P-201A stop, FIC-201 MAN 30 %; the column stays parked (loops in MAN)

res.obs: FI-201 0.1 → 54.1 m³/h at 00:03:42; P-201A quiet, PG-203A 2388 kPa g (it was 453 gas-bound); TIC-208 84.7 → 60.0 °C by 00:08:42 as the profile refills.
